name: Supabase

auth.keyHelp: Create a scoped token limited to your organization or project with only the read permissions you need (projects_read, organizations_read, database_read, edge_functions_read); avoid the Legacy full-access type.

write.label: Run SQL that can change data (read_only false)

tested: mock; real service refused a fake key
notes: Management API (api.supabase.com/v1), not the per-project data API. The intro page says to send the personal access token as a bearer token; its base URL is inferred from its example call rather than stated, and the token's visible prefix is not stated on the pages I read, so the field has no prefix hint. Scoped personal access tokens exist: a scoped token can only reach the organizations, projects and permissions picked at creation, with fine-grained permissions named in the reference pages (organizations_read, projects_read, database_read or database_write, edge_functions_read). Classic tokens, labelled Legacy in the dashboard, carry the user's full privileges, so tell the user to avoid them. A read-only key is therefore possible. The SQL query endpoint is marked experimental/Beta, accepts a read_only boolean in the body, and a token with database_read or database_write can call it (database:write OAuth scope). Whether database_read alone is rejected when read_only is false was not stated; the write action is listed but a database_read-only token might be refused or limited, so the read action uses POST /database/query/read-only, which runs as supabase_read_only_user and has no field that can turn that off. The 'who' path 0.name reads the first organization in the array returned by /v1/organizations because no endpoint here names the token owner. Rate limit is 120 requests per minute per user, project or organization and endpoint, shared across all of a user's tokens; some endpoints are stricter (30 per minute for analytics log queries). Official MCP server https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp uses OAuth by default; for CI a scoped PAT can be passed as a bearer header, and ?read_only=true and ?project_ref=<id> query parameters limit it. Not read: project-level API keys (anon/service role) which are a different credential.
